newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. envoy appeals to Afghans to stop fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy appeals to Afghans to stop fighting.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Norbert Holl, responding to fresh fighting in northern Afghanistan, appealed on Tuesday for a ceasefire and peace talks.

"In view of the new fighting...UNSMA (U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan) reiterates its appeal to the warring factions to stop the bloodshed and return to the negotiation table," Holl said in a statement issued in Islamabad.
"UNSMA will continue in its efforts to bring about an early ceasefire among the warring factions which could serve as the basis of a peaceful solution of the Afghanistan conflict...
"It appeals to all countries of influence to use their good offices to facilitate a negotiated settlement," Holl said.

General Abdu Malik, a key commander of northern opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, launched an uprising on Monday in favour of the Islamic Taleban militia that captured Kabul in September.

The United Nations has been trying without success to promote credible peace talks between the Taleban and a northern opposition alliance led by Dostum, ousted government commander Ahmad Shah Masood and a Shi'ite Moslem faction leader.
Holl said he had learned of the unrest in the north during a meeting with Masood in the northern city of Taloqan on Monday.
